name: Start event
meaning: The process begins here.
useWhen: Use exactly one to show what triggers the process.
commonMistake: Starting the diagram with a task box and no start event.

name: Message start event
meaning: The process begins when a message arrives.
useWhen: Use when something from outside starts the process.
commonMistake: Drawing an envelope when nothing is really received.

name: Timer start event
meaning: The process begins at a set time or on a schedule.
useWhen: Use for work that runs on a schedule.
commonMistake: Using it for a short wait in the middle; that is an intermediate timer.

name: Message intermediate event
meaning: The process waits in the middle for a message to arrive.
useWhen: Use when the flow must pause until a reply comes.
commonMistake: Using it to send mail; a send task says that better.

name: Timer intermediate event
meaning: The process waits in the middle until a time has passed.
useWhen: Use for a deadline or a pause.
commonMistake: Forgetting to draw what happens when the time runs out.

name: End event
meaning: This path of the process is finished.
useWhen: Use one for each way the process can finish.
commonMistake: Leaving a path with no end event.

name: Message end event
meaning: The path ends, and the last thing is a message sent out.
useWhen: Use when sending a final message is how the process finishes.
commonMistake: Using it when more work follows the message.

name: Terminate end event
meaning: The whole process stops now, on every path.
useWhen: Use to stop all parallel paths at once.
commonMistake: Using it where a normal end would let the other paths finish.

name: Task
meaning: One piece of work, without saying who or what does it.
useWhen: Use when the kind of worker does not matter yet.
commonMistake: Naming it with a noun, like Request, instead of a verb and an object.

name: User task
meaning: A person does the work, using a screen or a form.
useWhen: Use when a human has to act.
commonMistake: Using it for work that the system does by itself.

name: Service task
meaning: The system does the work by itself, such as a call to a service.
useWhen: Use for an automatic step.
commonMistake: Using it for work that a person has to do.

name: Send task
meaning: The task sends a message to someone outside the step.
useWhen: Use when the work is to send a message.
commonMistake: Mixing it up with the receive task, whose envelope is empty.

name: Receive task
meaning: The task waits until a message arrives.
useWhen: Use when the process cannot go on without a reply.
commonMistake: Drawing a filled envelope, which means send.

name: Collapsed sub-process
meaning: A group of steps hidden inside one box.
useWhen: Use to keep a big diagram short and readable.
commonMistake: Hiding steps that the reader needs to see.

name: Call activity
meaning: The step runs another process that is defined elsewhere and reused.
useWhen: Use when several processes share the same steps.
commonMistake: Copying the same steps into every diagram.

name: Exclusive gateway
meaning: Choose exactly one path.
useWhen: Use for a yes or no decision, or any choice of one.
commonMistake: Leaving the choices without labels.

name: Parallel gateway
meaning: Do all paths at the same time, and wait for all of them at the join.
useWhen: Use for work that can happen together.
commonMistake: Splitting with a plus and never joining.

name: Inclusive gateway
meaning: Choose one path or more than one.
useWhen: Use when any mix of the paths can be right.
example: Send the receipt by email, by SMS, or both
commonMistake: Using it when exactly one path is right.

name: Event-based gateway
meaning: Wait for the first of several events, and follow that path.
useWhen: Use when the outside world decides the path, such as a reply or a timeout.
example: Wait for the deposit or for 3 days to pass
commonMistake: Using an exclusive gateway when the path depends on which event comes first.

name: Sequence flow
shape: solid line with a filled arrowhead
meaning: Shows the order of the steps inside one pool.
useWhen: Use to connect events, tasks and gateways in order.
example: Submit event request, then Run the checks
commonMistake: Leaving a task with no incoming or no outgoing flow.

name: Message flow
shape: dashed line with an open circle at the start
meaning: Shows a message travelling between two pools.
useWhen: Use when two organizations or systems talk to each other.
example: Student Affairs sends the decision to the organizer
commonMistake: Using it between two tasks inside the same pool; use a sequence flow.

name: Association
meaning: Links a note or a data object to an element.
useWhen: Use to attach extra information, with no order implied.
example: The form linked to Submit event request
commonMistake: Using it to show the order of steps.

name: Pool
shape: large rectangle with a name band
meaning: One participant: an organization or a system with its own process.
useWhen: Use one pool for each organization that takes part.
commonMistake: Drawing two pools when everything happens inside one organization.

name: Lane
meaning: Shows who does each step inside a pool.
useWhen: Use to answer the question: who does it?
example: Organizer, Planner System, Student Affairs Officer
commonMistake: Leaving a task outside every lane.

name: Data object
meaning: Information that a task reads or writes.
useWhen: Use to show a document or a record that matters.
commonMistake: Treating it as a step; it is information, not work.

name: Annotation
meaning: A note that explains an element.
useWhen: Use to explain a rule that the shapes cannot show.
example: Only outdoor events need the weather check
commonMistake: Hiding a business rule in the note instead of the diagram.
